email.subject: Daily Journey: Walker Miles on www.skechers.com

review.raw_markdown:
--- ## Walker Miles — Skechers.com Mobile Journey Review **Date:** April 12, 2026 | **vs. Yesterday's Score: 4/10** --- ## 1. Executive Summary I'm a 62-year-old guy who just wants to find a good pair of slip-ins without fighting the website. Today's visit had some bright spots — the Men's nav menu is clean, the Slip-ins category page is exactly what I need — but the same old problems are still there. Homepage is pushing Mother's Day stuff at me, I never actually saw a login form, search dumped Women's shoes at me first, and worst of all: **the cart page was completely blank**. Can't buy what I can't see in my cart. This site is still leaving money on the table. --- ## 2. Business Impact Score: 4/10 **No change from yesterday.** The Men's navigation is genuinely good, and the product page is solid. But the broken cart is a conversion killer, search personalization is still missing, and the homepage treats me like I don't exist. Until the cart works reliably and the experience knows who I am, the score can't move. --- ## 3. What's Working - **Men's nav menu is clean and smart.** "Hands Free Slip-ins," "Wide Fit," and "Extra Wide Fit" are right there as direct links below the main categories. No hunting. That's exactly how you build a menu for someone like me. - **Slip-ins category page (Step 5) is well done.** Large "Hands Free Slip-ins" headline, clear description of the Heel Pillow tech, width filter buttons prominent at the top. 262 results shows real inventory. - **Product page text is readable.** The product name, price ($135.00), and BOGO deal are all in large, clear type. No squinting needed. The shoe image is big and tappable to swipe through. - **Add to Cart page is clean.** Size grid has reasonably large tap targets, the blue ADD TO CART button is massive and impossible to miss. The "Please select a size" warning is clear. - **BOGO 50% OFF banner is persistent.** It follows me through the whole journey in the top bar — I never forget there's a deal. That's good merchandising. --- ## 4. What's Weak - **Cart page is completely blank (Step 8).** Pure white screen. Nothing. If I added something to my cart and this is what I see, I'm calling my son to ask if the website is broken. This is a complete purchase blocker. Critical failure. - **Homepage is not for me (Step 1).** Full-screen Mother's Day shop, pink florals, a woman and her daughter. I have nothing against Mother's Day, but I'm a 62-year-old man looking for walking shoes. Nothing on that screen says "Walker, you're in the right place." - **Login was invisible (Step 3).** The screenshot for Step 3 looks identical to the homepage — same Mother's Day hero, no login form in sight. Either the login happened silently in the background (confusing) or it failed silently (worse). I have no confirmation I'm actually logged in. - **"Join Skechers Plus" shown to a member (Step 2).** After whatever login happened, the site tells me "Free Shipping with Skechers Plus — Join Now for free." I'm already a member. This should say "Welcome back, Walker" or "Your Plus benefits are active." Instead it's asking me to sign up for something I already have. Makes me feel like the site doesn't know who I am. - **Search returns Women's first (Step 9).** I searched "slip in" from within a Men's browsing session. The first two results are both Women's products. 1,021 results with zero auto-filtering to Men's. That's not helpful — that's a haystack. - **1,021 search results with no context filtering.** Even if the results were mixed by gender, 1,021 is overwhelming. No "did you mean Men's Slip-ins?" nudge. No pre-applied Men's filter based on my session context. --- ## 5. Recommendations 1. **Fix the cart page immediately.** A blank cart is a zero-revenue moment. This is priority one — no other improvement matters until someone can actually check out. 2. **Greet me by name when logged in.** My Skechers Plus status should be acknowledged on the homepage. "Welcome back, Walker — your BOGO deal is active" is worth real conversion lift. 3. **Stop showing me Mother's Day on the homepage.** Or at minimum, give me a secondary Men's banner below the hero. I shouldn't have to scroll past content aimed at women to find something relevant to me. 4. **Carry my browsing context into search.** If I've been in the Men's section all session, "slip in" search results should default-filter to Men's, or at least show Men's products first. 5. **Fix the Skechers Plus messaging post-login.** "Join Now for free" shown to an existing member erodes trust. It makes the logged-in state feel broken. --- ## 6. Bottom Line The bones of a good Men's shopping experience are here — the nav menu is genuinely well-organized for someone like me, and the Slip-ins category page delivers exactly what I came for. But a blank cart page means I literally cannot buy anything, and the site still doesn't know who I am after I log in. Same score as yesterday: **4/10**. Fix the cart, show me I'm logged in, and stop leading with content I have no interest in. --- ## 7. Evidence **Step 1 — Homepage** Landed on a full-screen Mother's Day Shop hero — woman and child, pink flowers, cursive text. Completely irrelevant to me. The top banner shows BOGO 50% OFF which is the one saving grace. Navigation is a hamburger MENU — small tap target in the corner, nothing that immediately says "Men's shoes this way." Not personalized at all. **Step 2 — Dismiss Popups** No visible popup to dismiss — the page just looks like the homepage with the sub-banner now reading "Free Shipping with Skechers Plus — Join Now for free." I'm a member and it's asking me to join. That's a miss. No friction from a popup at least, but the member messaging is wrong. **Step 3 — Log In** Screenshot is identical to the homepage. No login form visible, no confirmation of successful login, no welcome message, no name in the header. I have no idea if I'm logged in or not. The account icon in the header doesn't visibly change state. This is disorienting. **Step 4 — Men's Category Menu** This is the best screen of the journey. Clean list: Shoes, Shop by Activity, Comfort Technologies, Collections, Collaborations, Clothing & Accessories — all with clear chevron arrows. Below a divider, "Hands Free Slip-ins," "Wide Fit," "Extra Wide Fit" as flat direct links. Text is large enough to read. Touch targets feel comfortable. This menu knows what Men's shoppers like me want. **Step 5 — Men's Hands Free Slip-ins Page** Good page. Big headline. Clear tech copy about Heel Pillow. Width filter buttons (Wide, Extra Wide, Medium) are visible immediately — important for comfort shoppers. 262 results shown. Filter/Sort bar at bottom. I can see shoe cards starting to appear. Relevant, readable, appropriate. Minor issue: 262 results is still a lot without a "best for walking" sub-filter. **Step 6 — Product Page (Max Cushioning Arch Fit 2.0)** Text is large and clear — product name, "MEN'S" label, $135.00 price, 4-star rating with 11 reviews, and the BOGO deal prominently in red. Slip-ins badge is visible. Shoe image is large and swipeable. $135 made me pause — I'm price-conscious — but the BOGO deal softens it. Only 11 reviews is low confidence. Overall a readable, usable product page. **Step 7 — Add to Cart / Size Selection** Size grid is clear. Boxes are large enough to tap without too much fumbling. The "Please select a size" warning in red is appropriately prominent. QTY dropdown, Ship it / In-store options are listed below. The ADD TO CART button is a full-width blue bar — easy to find and tap. Solid page execution. **Step 8 — Cart Page** Completely blank. White screen. Nothing rendered. This is a critical failure — the worst screen of the entire journey. If this happened to me in real life, I'd assume the site crashed and give up. No product shown, no price, no checkout button, no BOGO confirmation. Revenue = $0. **Step 9 — Search Results ("slip in")** 1,021 results returned, which is too many. Header shows "SLIP IN" in large text — readable. But the first two visible product cards are both labeled "Women's." I'm a man who's been browsing Men's the whole time. The search ignored my context entirely. Filter and Sort are available, but I shouldn't have to re-filter to Men's after already being in that section. Relevant results exist — they're just buried. --- ## Technical Audit ## Technical Summary The skechers.com mobile journey shows structurally sound server response times but is undermined by: 30 axe violations (4 critical) concentrated on the product page, systematic 429 errors from Kasada's own bot-detection fingerprinting endpoint, a broken Stylitics widget due to CORS misconfiguration, and an extremely heavy third-party script payload with duplicate script loads. LCP and CLS were not captured for any step — a significant measurement gap. --- ## Accessibility **30 violations total; 4 critical, 6 serious.** **Critical (must fix):** - `image-alt` — `` elements missing `alt` on View Product. Fails WCAG 1.1.1. - `button-name` — buttons with no discernible text on View Product. Fails WCAG 4.1.2. - `aria-required-children` — ARIA role missing required child roles on View Product. Invalid ARIA tree. - `aria-valid-attr-value` — invalid ARIA attribute values on View Product. Likely `aria-*=""` or malformed IDs. **Serious:** - `link-name` (Homepage) — anchor elements with no accessible text; likely icon-only links with no `aria-label`. - `link-in-text-block` (Men's Shoes) — links distinguished only by color; fails WCAG 1.4.1. - `aria-dialog-name` (View Product) — modal/dialog missing `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`. - `aria-input-field-name` (View Product) — form inputs with ARIA roles but no accessible name. - `color-contrast` (View Product) — foreground/background fails WCAG AA ratio. **Moderate (structural, affects AT navigation):** - Duplicate `main` landmark (Homepage) — two `
` elements or nested landmark. - `landmark-complementary-is-top-level` on Homepage and Men's Shoes — `
` nested inside another landmark. - `heading-order` (Homepage) — heading levels skip (e.g., h1 → h3). The density of critical violations on View Product suggests the product detail page (likely a modal or SPA-injected overlay) was built without accessibility review. --- ## SEO **Third-party script volume is the primary SEO risk.** The page fires 20+ async third-party scripts before any meaningful content renders. While `async` prevents parser blocking, Googlebot's JavaScript rendering budget is finite — late-injected content (via Monetate, Bloomreach, etc.) may not be indexed. **Observed issues:** - Monetate loads two concurrent versions: `se.monetate.net/js/3/...` and `//se.monetate.net/js/2/...`. This is redundant and adds payload. - WebFontLoader (v1.6.28 from cdnjs) applies `wf-loading` class to `` during font resolution. If fonts are slow, text remains invisible — potential FOIT impacting perceived content completeness for crawlers. - The HTML snippet shows no `` or structured data in the visible fragment. Cannot confirm presence without full source. - `--vh` is computed server-side or early JS — not an SEO issue, but confirms layout depends on JS. --- ## Performance | Step | TTFB | LCP | CLS | Notes | |---|---|---|---|---| | Homepage | 34ms | ? | ? | | | Log In | 40ms | ? | ? | | | Men's Category | 40ms | ? | ? | | | Men's Shoes | 46ms | ? | ? | | | View Product | 29ms | ? | ? | | | Add to Cart | 29ms | ? | ? | | | View Cart | **147ms** | ? | ? | 3–5× spike; likely server-side cart recalculation | | Search | 91ms | ? | ? | | **TTFB is uniformly good** (well under 200ms) — CDN and origin are healthy. The View Cart 147ms spike is the only outlier and is on a critical conversion path. **LCP and CLS are not captured** — this is a critical gap. Without LCP, it is impossible to assess the largest contentful paint on a page with heavy above-the-fold images (hero banners, product imagery).
